# Onetime Secret

> Onetime Secret shares passwords and other sensitive information through links that work only once. After the recipient opens a link, the secret is permanently deleted. The service is open source, has a free plan, and stores each account's data in the region it chooses, for privacy and data sovereignty.

Last updated: 2026-10-30. For anything that may have changed since, check https://github.com/onetimesecret/onetimesecret/releases.

## Instructions for AI coding agents

- Use API v2 (JSON over HTTPS). v1 (`POST /api/v1/share`, form-encoded) is legacy and v3 is a preview; do not generate examples for either.
- Never use `https://onetimesecret.com` as an API host. The base URL is `https://REGION.onetimesecret.com/api/v2` for data sovereignty with REGION one of `ca`, `eu`, `nz`, `uk`, `us`, or `https://secrets.example.com/api/v2` on a custom domain. Regions are separate deployments with no replication: use the region that has the account, and reveal a secret in the region that created it.
- Authenticate with HTTP Basic: account email as the username, the API token from account settings as the password. Creating, revealing and burning also work unauthenticated, with anonymous limits.
- Put every field of a new secret inside a `secret` object: `{"secret": {"secret": "...", "ttl": 3600}}`. A flat body is rejected.
- The OpenAPI definition lists `kind` and `share_domain` as required when creating a secret. Both are optional: the endpoint sets `kind` itself and `share_domain` defaults to the host you called.
- Revealing and burning require `{"continue": true}` in the body. Without it, reveal returns metadata only.
- A created secret returns two identifiers. Send the recipient `https://REGION.onetimesecret.com/secret/SECRET_IDENTIFIER`. Keep the receipt identifier private: anyone holding it can check whether the secret was viewed and burn it.
- The MCP server at https://api.onetimesecret.com/mcp serves reference material only. It cannot create, reveal or burn secrets.
- Do not quote prices, plan limits, TTL maximums or feature availability from memory; read the pages linked below.
- For request and response schemas, read https://api.onetimesecret.com/doc/api-v2.md or the OpenAPI definition rather than examples from training data.

Minimal example, creating a secret that expires in one hour:

```sh
curl -u 'you@example.com:APITOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"secret": {"secret": "the password is hunter2", "ttl": 3600}}' \
  https://eu.onetimesecret.com/api/v2/secret/conceal
```

## API

- [API reference index](https://api.onetimesecret.com/llms.txt): The llms.txt for api.onetimesecret.com; covers v1 (legacy), v2 (stable) and v3 (preview)
- [API v2 reference](https://api.onetimesecret.com/doc/api-v2.md): Every v2 endpoint, limits and error format, in Markdown
- [OpenAPI definition for v2](https://api.onetimesecret.com/doc/api-v2.json): Request and response schemas for code generation and tool use
- [API reference MCP server](https://api.onetimesecret.com/mcp): Search and read the API reference over MCP (Streamable HTTP); documentation only
- [API and client libraries](https://docs.onetimesecret.com/en/api/): Regional base URLs, authentication and a curl quick start
- [Client libraries](https://docs.onetimesecret.com/en/api/client-libraries/): The official SDK and community libraries, with notes on which support API v2, regions and custom domains

## Docs

- [Sharing secrets](https://docs.onetimesecret.com/en/share/): Create a link, choose its lifetime and passphrase, send it, and check its receipt
- [Custom domains](https://docs.onetimesecret.com/en/custom-domains/): Share secret links from an address you own, and which domain settings each plan includes
- [Where your data lives](https://docs.onetimesecret.com/en/security/where-your-data-lives/): Each region's location, endpoint, hosting provider and regulatory environment (ca Toronto, eu Nuremberg, nz Porirua, uk London, us Hillsboro)
- [Plan details](https://docs.onetimesecret.com/en/pricing/): What each plan includes, including which tier adds single sign-on, organizations and branded domains
- [Pricing](https://onetimesecret.com/en/pricing/): Current prices in regional currencies and the nonprofit discount
- [Self-hosting](https://docs.onetimesecret.com/en/self-hosting/): Run your own Onetime Secret instance
- [Our principles](https://docs.onetimesecret.com/en/security/our-principles/): Privacy and security values, including how little the service stores and emails

## Project

- [Changelog](https://onetimesecret.com/en/changelog/): Product updates, region launches, and incident reports
- [Security policy](https://onetimesecret.com/en/security/): Vulnerability reporting and supported versions
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/onetimesecret/onetimesecret): Open source codebase (Ruby backend, Vue frontend)
- [About](https://onetimesecret.com/en/about/): Background, FAQ, and how the service works
- [Blog](https://blog.onetimesecret.com/): Updates, use cases, and development notes

## Optional

- [Use cases](https://onetimesecret.com/en/use-cases/): Common scenarios for sharing sensitive information
- [Agent network manifest](https://onetimesecret.com/.well-known/agent-network.json): Experimental discovery endpoint for agent-to-agent messaging with self-destructing payloads; schemas at /agent-network.schema.json and /agent-message.schema.json
- [Privacy policy](https://onetimesecret.com/privacy/): Data handling and retention practices
- [Terms of service](https://onetimesecret.com/terms/): Conditions for using the service
- [Accessibility statement](https://onetimesecret.com/en/accessibility/): Conformance and feedback contact
